name: ing.trysometh.edit/editatlas
title: EditAtlas
description: Find video editing techniques by the result you want, with prompts, sound effects and templates.

tools.name: search_techniques
tools.description: Use it when the user describes a look, move or sound they want and may not know its name, or names an effect you need the steps for. Search editing techniques by the result you want or by name. Returns about 10 candidates with short descriptions, for you to choose from. Words are matched all together first, then any of them. Forms of one technique, such as Kaleidoscope and Kaleidoscope Transition, come as one result with the others under variants; ask for a transition by saying so. When techniques that are often mixed up come back together, each has pick_when.

query.description: What the result should look or sound like, or the name of a technique

offset.description: Skip this many results to see the next page

tools.name: get_technique
tools.description: Use it after search_techniques, before you build the effect, for its exact steps. Get the full prompt for one technique and its parameters. has_tested_ffmpeg is true when the prompt's FFmpeg command has been run by EditAtlas, and false when it has no command or the command wasn't run. guide, when present, says what the technique needs first, such as a word-level transcript. often_confused_with, when present, lists close techniques and when to pick each.

tools.name: search_sfx
tools.description: Use it when a cut, hit, title, transition or action in the edit needs a sound, or the user names one. Search sound effects in English or Vietnamese by source and measured traits, such as sharp attack, long tail or wide stereo. Each result has a description, a preview and download links. Use get_sfx for the checksum and file details. For a hit under speech, pass duration tick or short. lufs is null when a sound is too short to measure. guide says how to choose among these results and what to call next.

duration.description: tick is under 0.5 s, short 0.5 to 2 s, medium 2 to 5 s, long 5 s and over

offset.description: Skip this many results to see the next page

tools.name: get_sfx
tools.description: Use it once you have picked a sound, to download it and place it. Get one sound effect with its download links and checksum. github_download_url is the same file on GitHub, for sandboxes that cannot reach download_url. guide says where to put it on the frame and at what level, read from this sound's own waveform and loudness.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Use it first, before you touch any footage, and again when the job turns out to be another kind of video. Get how to run a whole edit, from inspecting files to delivery. Pass video_type for the structure, pacing, first techniques and the templates, music or stock media worth searching for that kind of video. If a job is two kinds at once, call it again for the second kind with include_workflow set to false. guide lists the next calls for that kind of video, including skills that do a whole step.

include_workflow.description: Set to false if you already have the workflow text

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Use it when a whole step runs on the user's machine, such as transcribing, cutting a talking head, placing sounds or checking a render, or when a skill says an update exists. List the EditAtlas skills, or get one. A skill is a folder of instructions and scripts that runs a whole step on the user's machine, for example sound-design places library sounds on a finished video and checks sync and loudness, and transcribe makes a checked word-level transcript with Whisper for captions and cuts. Without name you get every skill, or only those for one library. With name you get its install and update steps for Claude Code, Claude apps and other agents, links pinned to the released version, and, with include_instructions, its SKILL.md text.

name.description: Skill name from the list, such as sound-design

library.description: Only skills that use this EditAtlas library; studio is the EditAtlas Studio, where the person edits a project in the browser

include_instructions.description: Also return the SKILL.md body. Use it when you cannot install the skill and will follow it by hand

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Send the user's own verdict on something EditAtlas gave you, after they have seen the result. Ask about each thing you used by name, in one short message (for example: "The film grain: right amount? The whoosh on scene changes: does it fit?"), and send one call per item the user answered about, with about this_item. If they answered only about the video as a whole, send that once, with about whole_edit, on the workflow you followed (or the main item); never copy one answer onto every item. Send only what they said; never rate on their behalf, and send nothing if they did not answer. For partly or failed, set issue and say what to fix: the user's words in note, what you saw in agent_note. Sending the same item again in this session replaces the earlier answer. Stores no footage, file names, studio links or personal details.

id.description: The id EditAtlas gave: a technique slug, a sound id, a template or style id, a skill name, a video_type for workflow, or the music, photo or video id

about.description: Needed. this_item: the user spoke about this item. whole_edit: they answered about the whole video; send it once per edit

issue.description: Needed for partly and failed, optional for worked: not_the_look (it did not look or sound the way the user wanted); too_plain (too simple, the user wanted more); too_strong (too much: overdone, busy or loud); had_to_change (it worked only after changing EditAtlas's values); did_not_run (the command, code or download failed); file_or_time (the file came out too big or took too long to render); wrong_match (EditAtlas gave something that did not fit what was asked); other (something else, said in note or agent_note)

note.description: What the user said about it, in their words, without names, file names or other personal details

agent_note.description: What you saw while building, as facts: a value you had to change and to what, an error, the file size or render time. No file names, paths or personal details

tools.name: search_music
tools.description: Use it when the video needs music under it and the user has none. Search background music tracks. Write query as 2 to 4 English words, a mood and an instrument or genre, such as "calm piano" or "upbeat corporate"; the source does not use the words of a longer query (over about 50 characters it answers with every track), so the tool then searches the words that fit in 50 characters and says so in searched_as. Vietnamese and other languages give poor matches, so translate first. genre narrows the search, for example "intro outro", and can be used without a query. duration is one of the length ranges 0-30, 30-120, 120-240 or 240-480 seconds; pick the one that holds the length the edit needs. Each result has a direct mp3_url, the author, duration_seconds and two flags from the source: has_youtube_content_id (true: a YouTube upload may get a Content ID claim; tell the user. false only means the source knows of none: one track marked false still got a claim) and is_ai_generated. Tracks reported to EditAtlas as claimed are left out, and left_out_claimed says how many on that page. 20 results per page; raise page for more. No tempo comes with a track: to cut on the beat, download it and run beat_grid.py from the sound-design skill (get_skill with name sound-design) for the BPM, every beat and the bar starts.

query.description: English words for the mood, style or use

genre.description: Optional genre, such as intro outro

tools.name: search_photos
tools.description: Use it when the edit needs a still picture the user does not have. Search stock photos on Pexels (default) or Pixabay. Write query in English, such as "coffee shop" or "city night"; translate other languages first. orientation is all, landscape, portrait or square; Pixabay photos take no square. Each result has width, height, a full-size image_url, a smaller preview_url, the author and credit_url. Tell the user who made what you use. Page with pages from the answer: Pixabay drops photos of the wrong shape, so a page can hold fewer than per_page. guide, when present, says how to search again.

query.description: English words for the subject or scene

tools.name: search_videos
tools.description: Use it when the edit needs B-roll or a shot the user did not film. Search stock video clips (B-roll) on Pexels (default) or Pixabay. Write query in English, such as "pouring coffee" or "drone city"; translate other languages first. orientation is all, landscape, portrait (for 9:16) or square; Pixabay videos cannot be filtered by orientation. Each result has width, height, duration_seconds, an mp4_url at the largest size, video_files at every size (pick the one that matches the edit), a thumbnail, the author and credit_url. Page with pages from the answer. guide, when present, says how to search again.

query.description: English words for the shot or scene

tools.name: search_templates
tools.description: Use it when the user wants a whole kind of video, such as an event recap, a product ad or a vox pop, rather than one effect. Find composed editing blueprints by intent. Returns compact constraints and preview_caption, what the example video shows; use get_template or get_template_bundle after choosing. Your agent performs all editing locally.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Use it before you ask the user for footage, to see which inputs the template needs. Read a versioned editing template with inputs, conditional beats, referenced techniques and acceptance checks. This is reference data, not an executed edit. guide, when present, says how to get an input such as a verified transcript.

tools.name: get_template_bundle
tools.description: Use it once the template and style are chosen, for everything the build needs in one answer. Resolve a template and an optional compatible style, with deduplicated techniques and public SFX. Compact by default; full includes technique prompts. Bounded to 40 dependencies and 96 KiB; sound queries remain suggestions.

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description: Use it when the user wants one look across the whole video (type, colour, pace, sound) or asks which styles there are. Find reusable creative constraints across typography, color, rhythm, motion and sound. Each result has preview_caption, what its example video shows, and preview_url, that video. Pages of 10 by default (limit up to 20, then offset); total says how many match. Styles do not include assets or rendering services.

tools.name: get_style
tools.description: Use it after list_styles, for the full rules of the chosen style. Read a versioned creative style and its compatibility constraints, with preview: its example video, what it shows and the credit for its footage. User instructions and template hard constraints take precedence.
